aboutAuthor: Jason Fried and David Heinemeier Hansson founded Basecamp (37signals), a profitable software company run entirely remotely. Rework challenges nearly every conventional rule of starting and running a business.

points.heading: Planning is guessing
points.body: Long business plans are fiction dressed up in spreadsheets. Markets change too fast for five-year forecasts to mean anything. Decide in the moment, act on the best information you have now, and call it what it is — guessing.

points.heading: Start a business, not a startup
points.body: You don't need venture capital, an exit strategy, or a garage myth. A real business pays its own bills from day one. Building a company you want to run forever beats building one designed to be sold.

points.heading: Make a dent in your niche
points.body: You don't need to be world-changing to matter. Outdo an incumbent by doing what they do, minus what they get wrong. Having direct competitors is fine — just carve out the part of the market that cares about what you uniquely offer.

points.heading: Underdo the competition
points.body: Feature wars are a losing game. Solve the simple problems and leave the hard ones to others. Basecamp beat bloated project-management suites by doing less — customers paid for simplicity, not checklists of features.

points.heading: Meetings are toxic
points.body: A one-hour meeting with eight people costs eight hours of productivity. Meetings interrupt work, breed more meetings, and rarely produce decisions that a well-written document couldn't. Communicate asynchronously and reserve gatherings for genuine decisions.

points.heading: Inspiration is perishable
points.body: Ideas lose freshness fast — strike while they're hot. Launch now, iterate publicly, and let real usage teach you what planning never could. Done is better than perfect because perfection is just procrastination in disguise.

insights: Basecamp has been profitable every year since launch without raising venture capital.
The book itself was produced the way it prescribes: written in short bursts, shipped before it felt 'finished.'
'Hiring' is the chapter most founders say changed how they staffed their companies.
conclusion: Rework replaces startup theater with quiet, durable business craft: stay small, charge money, write instead of meeting, and ship before inspiration expires. Ignore the noise, do the work, and let a profitable little company fund the life you actually want.
